title: Existence of a Ruler Device
statement: There exist a finite state set $P$ with decidable equality, a one-work-tape Boolean Turing machine $R$ with state set $P$, states $readEntry,moveExit\in P$, an injective map $readExit:\mathrm{Option}(\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\})\to P$ whose image excludes $moveExit$, a map $moveEntry:\{-1,0,1\}\to P$, and a constant $C\in\mathbb N$ with the following property. For any Boolean words $y,z$, any $\ell$ with $0<\ell\le |z|$, any configuration $d$ of $R$ on input $z$, and any input-head position $i$ among the $|y|+2$ positions, suppose deleting the first $\ell$ symbols of $z$ gives $y$, the input head of $d$ is at $\ell+i$, and its work tape at every offset $p$ from $-1$ through $\ell$ from its head contains the corresponding cell of the tape encoding $\ell$ true symbols. If $d$ is in state $readEntry$, then within $C(\ell+1)$ steps the machine reaches the otherwise unchanged configuration with state $readExit(inputCell(y,i))$; before that time it does not enter any $readExit$ state, and throughout the run its work head stays within distance $\ell+1$ of its initial position. For every movement sign $m$, if $d$ is in state $moveEntry(m)$, then within $C(\ell+1)$ steps it reaches state $moveExit$, with input head at $\ell+moveInputPos(i,m)$, unchanged work tape, work-head position, and output; before that time it does not enter $moveExit$, and throughout the run its work head stays within distance $\ell+1$ of its initial position.

replaced:
There exist a finite state set $P$ with decidable equality, a deterministic
one-work-tape Turing machine $R$ over the Boolean alphabet, states
$readEntry,moveExit\in P$, an injective map $readExit:\mathrm{Option}(\{0,1\})\to P$
whose image excludes $moveExit$, a map $moveEntry:\{-1,0,1\}\to P$, and a constant
$C\in\mathbb N$ with the following property. For any Boolean words $y,z$, any $\ell>0$
with $\ell\leq |z|$ and suffix $z$ after deleting its first $\ell$ symbols equal to $y$,
any configuration $d$ of $R$ on input $z$ whose input head is at $\ell+i$ and whose work
tape, from one cell left of its head through $\ell$ cells to its right, contains the
encoding of $\ell$ true symbols, and any input-head position $i$ among the $|y|+2$
positions, the following hold: if $d$ is in state $readEntry$, then within $C(\ell+1)$
steps the machine reaches the otherwise unchanged configuration with state $readExit$ of
the input cell at position $i$ in the boundary-blank convention; before that time it
does not enter any $readExit$ state, and throughout the run its work head stays within
distance $\ell+1$ of its initial position. For every movement sign $m$, if $d$ is in
state $moveEntry(m)$, then within $C(\ell+1)$ steps it reaches state $moveExit$, its
input head is at $\ell$ plus the clamped move of $i$ by $m$, and its work tape,
work-head position, and output are unchanged; before that time it does not enter
$moveExit$, and throughout the run its work head stays within distance $\ell+1$ of its
initial position.
